title: Test equipment and measurements
blurb: Choose the right meter or scope for each station measurement and explain how a two-tone test and antenna analyzer work.

G4B01.why: An oscilloscope draws a trace using a **vertical** amplifier for amplitude and a **horizontal** one for the time sweep.
G4B01.trap: Meters and signal generators have no deflection channels.

G4B02.why: A DVM gives one number. A scope shows how voltage **changes over time**, so it can display **complex waveforms**.
G4B02.trap: A DVM is the more precise of the two.

G4B03.why: Keying is a **shape** (rise, hold, fall), and only an oscilloscope shows shape.
G4B03.trap: A sidetone monitor only lets you hear it; a field strength meter gives a level.

G4B04.why: The scope watches the transmitter's **own RF output**, attenuated to a safe level, to see the envelope.
G4B04.trap: Oscillator and mixer signals are internal, not what is transmitted.

G4B05.why: A high-impedance meter draws almost no current, so it **barely loads the circuit** and the reading stays true.
G4B05.trap: Impedance is about loading, not range or resolution.

G4B06.why: A digital meter reads to more digits, so it gives **higher precision**.
G4B06.trap: Analog needles respond faster to changes.

G4B07.why: Two tones that aren't harmonics of each other beat to a repeating envelope that exposes distortion: **two non-harmonically related audio signals**.

G4B08.why: A distorted envelope in a two-tone test means the amplifier isn't amplifying proportionally: it tests **linearity**.
G4B08.trap: Carrier and sideband suppression are separate checks.

G4B09.why: A moving needle makes it easy to see a peak or dip while you adjust, so use analog when **adjusting for maximum or minimum**.

G4B10.why: Forward and reflected power give the reflection coefficient, and from it the **SWR**.
G4B10.trap: Pattern and propagation need antenna tests, not an inline wattmeter.

G4B11.why: The analyzer makes its own test signal, so it needs **only the antenna and feed line**.

G4B12.why: Strong outside signals enter the analyzer's receiver and **corrupt the SWR reading**.

G4B13.why: An analyzer measures impedance, SWR and related line properties, including the **impedance of coax**. It doesn't measure gain, pattern or transmitter power.
G4B13.trap: Gain and front-to-back need field measurements.
